sections.presenting_complaint: Flare of rheumatoid arthritis for 3 weeks.
sections.history: Painful swelling of the right wrist and right hand knuckles for 3 weeks. Early morning stiffness lasting about 30 minutes. Mild foot ache. Mild nausea the day after methotrexate. No sore throat, fever, bruising, cough or breathlessness. Drinks about 6 units of alcohol a week. Had shingles last month.
sections.medications_allergies: Methotrexate 15 mg once weekly (Mondays). Folic acid 5 mg once weekly (Thursdays). Sulfasalazine: rash.
sections.examination: Synovitis of the right wrist and right 2nd and 3rd MCP joints. Left hand normal. Chest clear on auscultation. Bloods: CRP 28, FBC and LFTs normal. DAS28 4.8.
sections.impression: Rheumatoid arthritis flare, moderate disease activity on methotrexate.
sections.plan: Increase methotrexate to 20 mg once weekly (Mondays); continue folic acid 5 mg once weekly (Thursdays). Intramuscular methylprednisolone 120 mg today. Bloods every 2 weeks for 6 weeks, then 3-monthly. Clinic review in 3 months.
sections.safety_netting: Report a painful blistering rash promptly.
